newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank bid rejection could mean yield cap.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank bid rejection could mean yield cap.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland rejected all bids at Wednesday's tender of NBP-bills, available only to Polish banks, signalling that it was not likely to accept higher yields for its longer bills, dealers said.
On Wednesday the central bank did not accept any of the 816 million zlotys of bids at its 700 million tender of 182-day and 273-day NBP-bills, which both last yielded 22.00 percent.
"Probably 182-day and 273-day NBP-bills will hold around 22.00 percent and would not rise in line with yields on shorter paper," said Andrzej Hirsz, senior dealer at Bank Gdanski SA .
Last week the central bank increased the average yield on its 91-day NBP-bills by 0.15 to 22.15 percent, a move followed by a steep increase of T-bill yields at Tuesday's tender.
Dealers said this sharp increase in T-bill yields may have caused players to bid for higher NBP-bill yields today.

"It may have been a question of price...that banks were bidding for much higher yields, but it signals that T-bills are a good investment because NBP-bill yields seem capped," said Andrzej Ladko, chief dealer at Bank Handlowy SA. @
"It is a good time to start buying T-bills because they have about the same yields as NBP-bills but are more liquid and very attractive for clients," Ladko said.

Dealers also said that when NBP-bill yields were less than half a point above comparable treasury yields banks would choose T-bills because they were more liquid and eligible as lombard loan collateral.
They said however, that the central bank would have to hold another NBP-bill tender to confirm that yields had peaked because no new yield levels were established on Wednesday.
The central bank would not comment on the results of the Wednesday auction.

At the Treasury's Tuesday T-bill auction the maximum yield of the benchmark 52-week bill increased to 21.86 percent from 21.50 percent last week, while the maximum 13- and 26-week yields rose to 21.79 and 21.90 percent respectively.
